surface_mechanism_description: According to the adsorbate inhibition model, alkyl radicals are considered to be attached to group-III atoms after a group-III source supply. After a H2 purge and group-V source supply, the alkyl radicals are readily removed from the surface by the reaction with a group-V source. If the alkyl radicals could not be removed, they would stay on the surface and be incorporated into epilayers.
